bull.b: The sharp increase in bookings and pipeline indicates expanding customer interest and a broader commercial opportunity. If converted into revenue, this backlog can support growth across system sales, cloud services and professional services over the next several quarters.

A larger enterprise customer base and higher commercial revenue mix suggest the company is moving beyond research users toward repeatable business adoption. Production deployments can improve credibility, create reference accounts, and support durable expansion across industries.

The combination of established annealing technology and an emerging gate-model roadmap broadens the addressable use cases. Partnerships with enterprise, telecom and semiconductor organizations can accelerate deployment, validate performance and strengthen D-Wave's ecosystem position.

bear.b: Heavy cash consumption and large operating losses show that the business is not yet self-funding. Continued investment may be necessary to reach commercial scale, but prolonged deficits could reduce financial flexibility and require further capital before profitability is achieved.

Expense growth substantially ahead of revenue places pressure on operating leverage and makes margin improvement dependent on rapid commercialization. Unless bookings convert efficiently into revenue, elevated product development and go-to-market spending can prolong losses.

The decline in available liquidity increases the importance of disciplined spending and successful revenue execution. Although potential CHIPS funding could support development, its milestone-based and unpaid status means it cannot yet offset the company's ongoing cash requirements.
